_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES: even 0-based indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. idx 0 is the bilingual cover, idx 1 the Hindi General Instructions, and idx 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 are HINDI-ONLY (p13 confirmed at full size: the Hindi Q12 (ङ) carrying the same lens figure). No English overflow sits at the top of any odd page. Every page of the 15 accounted for. The English content is CONTINUOUS with no gap — p04 ends at Q4(c) and p06 opens at Q5; p06 ends at Q7(b)(ii)(II) and p08 opens at Q8; p08 ends at Q11 and p10 opens at SECTION C; p10 ends at Q12(a) option (iv) and p12 opens at Q12(b); p12 ends at Q12(d) and p14 carries Q12(e) — so every question 1-12 and every printed sub-part is present on the even pages and nothing could be stranded on an odd one. DECIMAL POINTS ARE RAISED throughout the paper (3·27 MeV, 2·56 × 10⁻¹², 6·0 cm, 3·0 cm, 4·0 cm) and are written {\cdot}; the marking scheme MIXES raised and ordinary dots, and the PAPER is followed. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (vi) prints no count, so the roster was built by walking the whole marking scheme for a bare OR on its own line and confirming each against a printed OR on the English page and अथवा on the Hindi one — exactly THREE, at Q1, Q7 and Q10. VOIDS: the complete 12-page marking scheme was read (p00-p01 examiner instructions, p02-p11 answers) and it carries NO void note, NO award-regardless note, NO dual key and NO medium-specific clause of any kind. SECTION-C KEYS: Q12(a)-(e) are five 1-mark MCQs and the scheme keys all five in its Section-C block on ms/p11, printed as '(a) (iv) …', '(b) (iv) virtual and formed in air', '(c) (i) real and of the size of the object', '(d) (ii) + 5D', '(e) (iii) f'; options are printed (i)-(iv) and are mapped POSITIONALLY onto A-D, giving D, D, A, B, C. Those five keys are taken verbatim — none is derived.

questions.stem:
Answer the following, giving reason :
(a) The resistance of a p-n junction is low when it is forward biased and is high when it is reversed biased.
(b) Doping of intrinsic semiconductors is a necessity for making electronic devices.
(c) Photodiodes are operated in reverse bias.
questions._flag: Three parts spanning three subtopics of one chapter — (a) junction biasing, (b) doping / extrinsic semiconductors, (c) the photodiode. Filed on the dominant one, since (a) and (c) both turn on the biasing of a junction. All three subtopics exist on the live axis (including Special Purpose p-n Junction Diodes), so this is a span, not a gap. The stem is transcribed as printed, including the paper's 'reversed biased' where 'reverse biased' is meant.

questions.subtopic: Refraction at Spherical Surfaces and by Lenses
questions.context: Two transparent media of refractive indices \(\mathrm{n_1}\) and \(\mathrm{n_2}\) are separated by a spherical transparent surface. The rays of light incident on the surface get refracted into the medium on the other side. The laws of refraction are valid at each point of the spherical surface. A lens is a transparent optical medium bounded by two surfaces, at least one of which should be spherical. The focal length of a lens is determined by the radii of curvature \((\mathrm{R_1}\) and \(\mathrm{R_2})\) of its two surfaces and the refractive index (n) of the medium of the lens with respect to the surrounding medium. Depending on \(\mathrm{R_1}\) and \(\mathrm{R_2}\), a lens behaves as a diverging or a converging lens. The ability of a lens to diverge or converge a beam of light incident on it defines its power.
questions.stem: An object is placed at the point B as shown in the figure. The object distance (u) and the image distance (v) are related as
questions._figure: REQUIRED — and the figure IS the discriminator, so it is described only in part. The point B the stem names exists ONLY in the drawing, and which of the two media the object sits in is exactly what chooses between the four options. READ ON PAGE idx 10 OF THIS PAPER: a spherical refracting surface drawn across two parallel horizontal boundary lines, the region on one side of it labelled \(n_1\) and the region on the other \(n_2\), the annotation \((n_2 > n_1)\) printed beside the axis, a horizontal principal axis carrying two dotted points labelled C and B, and two dimension arrows below it labelled R (from the surface's vertex to C) and u (from that vertex to B). WITHHELD: which side of the surface each of C, B, \(n_1\) and \(n_2\) lies on, and hence the direction the light travels. Page idx 10.
